title: How To Lock-In Your Classroom Management Plan
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin describes a single high-leverage move for cementing a classroom management plan after the initial teaching, modeling, and practicing of the first week: watching for the end of the honeymoon period and then stopping class cold to reteach the plan with greater intensity. He explains that the honeymoon typically ends around the third week of school, signaled by subtle testing such as sloppy routines or a loss of urgency, and that most teachers make the mistake of backing off right when standards start to slip. His concrete technique is to clear the schedule for 10-15 minutes the moment testing appears, pause briefly, and reteach the plan from the beginning with bolder intention, more direct language, and higher expectations than the first time. The argument underneath the technique is that students secretly want structure and purpose, and that reasserting the plan at this critical moment proves to them the teacher's word is permanent, which produces lasting buy-in rather than resentment.
points: Watch for the honeymoon period to end, typically around the third week, signaled by subtle testing like sloppy routines or lost urgency.
The moment testing appears, stop everything, clear 10-15 minutes, and reteach the plan with bolder, more vehement clarity than the first time.
Most teachers make the mistake of backing off when the honeymoon ends, which trains students to expect standards to slide every year.
Reasserting the plan with force proves to students that the teacher's word is permanent, which students actually crave despite testing it.
Once locked in, students experience an exhilaration from excellence that nothing else in their daily lives can replicate.
quotes: Well, the first step is to watch for the honeymoon period to end. You’ll know it’s over when you start to notice mild testing—subpar routines, loss of focus, or general lack of urgency.
The moment this happens be ready to stop whatever you’re doing and clear the schedule for the next 15 minutes. If your students are up and about, send them back to their seats.
This is critical because most teachers back off when the honeymoon period ends. Their boundaries sag and weaken. Their standards slide. They allow sloppiness and mild testing.

And here’s the best part: They’ll embrace it. Because deep down, they want it. Despite social media, cultural rot, and all that conspires to bring kids down into failure and discontent, they all want to be part of something special.
But you must force it upon them. You must overcome their resistance and teach it in bold detail. You must demand it, expect it, and never, ever let it go.
